headline: Microsoft to Pay Top Cloud Workers More, Crack Down on Others
author: Brody Ford

paragraphs.text: Fri, November 20, 2026 at 12:05 PM CST 2 min read
(Bloomberg) -- Microsoft Corp. is making pay more performance-based in its crucial cloud division, the latest tech industry attempt to push employees to work even harder.

Those employees who receive top marks will get additional stock awards while workers with lower results will have formal meetings with their managers, according to a memo sent by Arun Ulagaratchagan, executive vice president at the Azure cloud computing division.

"Pay-for-performance only works if we are equally rigorous on both sides: recognizing exceptional impact and being honest when performance falls short," Ulagaratchagan wrote in the memo, which was reviewed by Bloomberg News.

Many big tech companies are pushing employees to do more, including by more regularly axing those they deem low performers. Microsoft has shed tens of thousands of workers in waves of layoffs in recent years, and is currently offering buyouts to about 60,000 of its employees.

"A world-class team like Azure requires world-class talent," a Microsoft spokesperson said Friday. "Yesterday, we shared an update to our compensation model in Azure, which includes meaningful additional awards for our strongest performing colleagues. We also shared an update on how we will ensure employees have clear expectations and receive timely, direct feedback from their managers."

Elon Musk in 2022 famously gave Twitter employees the choice to be "extremely hardcore," or take a severance payment. Earlier this year, Business Insider reported that an executive at Alphabet Inc.'s Google told employees in his organization that those who weren't "all in" on AI could have a voluntary buyout package.

"Meeting today's bar means closing previous performance gaps and demonstrating a meaningful step-change in impact," Ulagaratchagan wrote. "AI is reshaping how the world works, and competition has never been more intense."
